items.description: No module outside app/repositories/ issues any database session call (ORM-only contract: persistence is exclusively owned by the repository layer)
app/services/ contains no SQLAlchemy or ORM import statements (the service must not touch the ORM directly)
app/routes/ contains no SQLAlchemy or ORM import statements (the boundary must not touch the ORM directly)
No hardcoded database connection string exists anywhere in the application source tree; DATABASE_URL is read exclusively from the environment (twelve-factor config-from-env, NFR-F1-7)
app/routes/ contains no server-side template rendering in any route handler; the boundary returns JSON only (NFR-F1-5)
The stock_records Alembic migration completes a single-step downgrade followed by a single-step upgrade against the real branch database without error (reversibility, PI5)
Rows seeded into stock_records before the migration upgrade are still present with their original field values after the upgrade completes against the real branch database (data-preservation, PI5)
POSTing a valid stock filing with a uuid-suffixed SKU to the JSON API persists a row in the branch database containing the exact SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code that were submitted
A direct INSERT to stock_records with any required NOT NULL column (sku, location, inventory_code, or quantity) set to NULL is rejected by the real branch database (PI2)
A direct INSERT to stock_records with quantity less than zero is rejected by the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint on the real branch database (PI3)
The service layer raises a rejection before any database call is issued when a filing request carries a quantity below zero (service-layer write-time guard, NFR-F1-2)
A filing request with an invalid field value produces an error payload that names the specific offending field rather than returning a generic error message (NFR-F1-6)
GETting a previously filed stock record via the JSON API returns the exact quantity and inventory_code that were originally filed, without any transformation or truncation
Filing stock for an existing (sku, location) pair via the JSON API returns a success response with no error surfaced (AC3 collision — no error page)

After filing stock for an existing (sku, location) pair via the JSON API, the branch database contains exactly one row for that pair with the quantity and inventory_code from the second filing (no duplicate stored)
Filing a second stock record for an already-stored (sku, location) pair produces exactly one stock_records row for that key in the real branch database (unique constraint PI1)

Two concurrent transactions each attempting to upsert a stock_records row for the same (sku, location) key produce exactly one row for that key in the real branch database (transactional atomicity, PI4)
The created_at value of an existing stock_records row is unchanged after an in-place upsert that updates the quantity and inventory_code on the same row (audit-timestamp immutability, NFR-F1-1)
